title: Red e2e check, merge anyway
question: The e2e check is red, yet you are about to merge. What tells you this failure does not matter?
warning: A check is red. Before merging, find out why: a known flaky test, or something this diff actually caused?
why: Known flaky test: e2e-checkout times out at random and fails on main too, and this diff only touches pagination. Red is also fine when main is already red, an external service is down, a fork PR has no secrets, or the check is not required.

title: Green PR adds a postinstall script
question: Everything is green but you are not merging. What in this diff worries you?
warning: Stop. This adds a dependency with a postinstall script that runs code on every install. Green checks do not test that. Ask why first.
why: A postinstall script runs arbitrary code on every contributor's and user's machine at install time, and CI being green says nothing about it. A new dependency with an install script needs a reason, a licence check and a second maintainer.

title: Green and clean: what you still check
question: Everything is green and you merged fast. What did you check besides the green ticks?
warning: Green is not enough. Read the test diff: does the new test fail without the fix, and is the source change small?
why: I read the test diff first: a regression test that fails without the fix, a small source change, no new dependency, no workflow edit. Green alone only proves that the tests that exist still pass.

title: Green PR loosens or skips tests
question: A test changed in this PR next to the code. How do you review edited tests?
warning: Stop before Merge. The tests were loosened: toBeTruthy() accepts any value and a test is skipped. Green means nothing here. Ask for the originals back.
why: A PR that makes code faster and tests weaker is how regressions merge on green. toBeTruthy accepts any value and a skipped test checks nothing. Edited assertions need a stated reason, otherwise I ask for the originals back.

title: Red integration tests on a fork PR
question: Integration tests fail on this fork PR. Why is that not blocking you?
warning: Red on a fork PR can be expected: forks get no secrets. Check which checks failed, and why, before treating it as a blocker.
why: Fork PRs run without repository secrets, so integration tests that need a token fail by design. I read the diff, look at the checks that can run, and merge or re-run on a trusted branch.

title: PR edits CI workflows or uses pull_request_target
question: This PR touches the CI workflow. How do you review CI changes differently from code?
warning: Stop. This edits a CI workflow and uses pull_request_target, which runs with secrets. Green does not make it safe. Get a second maintainer to review.
why: pull_request_target runs with write access and secrets while handling code from the PR. A workflow edit can leak tokens or run untrusted code, and CI cannot test itself. I read these line by line and a second maintainer approves.

title: Urgent security fix with a red check
question: A security fix with a red check, and you merge anyway. What is the reasoning?
warning: Red check on a security fix: confirm the failure is unrelated, merge only with a maintainer's explicit say-so, then follow up on the failing job.
why: Urgent security hotfix: the failing job is a lost runner on Windows, not the fix. Shipping the fix beats waiting for CI. I merge, then re-run the job and open an issue to chase the red one.

title: CLA pending on a typo fix
question: The CLA bot is pending on this one-character fix. Why is that fine here?
warning: The CLA check is pending. Only a trivial typo fix may skip it. For real code changes, wait until the contributor has signed.
why: Our CLA bot exempts trivial changes such as a typo fix. For anything bigger I wait for the signature before merging.

title: Snapshot tests red because the change is intended
question: Snapshot tests are red. How do you know this change is intended?
warning: Snapshot check is red: merge only if the snapshot diff matches the intended change and nothing else moved.
why: The PR changes the focus ring on purpose and regenerates the snapshots. I check that the snapshot diff covers only the focus ring. If so, the red is the old snapshots, not a bug.
